resolutions.finding: Missing 48 - ScrollActivity and ScrollActivityReporter (RenderBudget.swift:11-75) have no requirement in any spec file, while SETTINGS specifies only the reporter side and UPDATE requires the sparkle canvas to pause on the flag. Owner: SETTINGS or a shared UI area.
resolutions.truth: RenderBudget.swift:11-75 is unspecified and the dependency runs both ways through my files: PR-SETTINGS-019 cites SettingsScrollTracker.swift:25/:35/:54 calling setScrolling, and PR-UPDATE-110 / UI-UPDATE-009 require pausing on ScrollActivity.shared.isScrolling (AboutUpdateViews.swift:457, and :371 for the slider itself, covered elsewhere in UPDATE). Source read in full: isScrolling is private(set) and derived from a Set<UUID> (:16-17, :41-43); reporters live in [UUID: WeakReporter] with a weak object (:22, :25-27); setScrolling inserts id + reporter on true and removes BOTH on false, reporter defaulting to nil (:29-39); a watchdog Task is created only when the flag has just become true and watch is nil, sleeps 2 seconds BEFORE its first check, sweeps a copy of the set dropping ids whose weak reporter is gone or whose isScrollingNow is false, republishes the union and clears its own handle and returns once the set empties (:44-63); the union going false cancels the task and nils the handle (:64-67); the protocol is class-bound, main-actor, single member `var isScrollingNow: Bool { get }` (:72-75).
resolutions.action_taken: Added five requirements to SETTINGS.json, one per atomic behaviour: PR-SETTINGS-260 (the flag is the union over reporting timelines, so one scrolling pane pauses motion app-wide, and it is written only on a real change so an observer re-renders at most twice per scroll), -261 (setScrolling's symmetric insert/remove of id AND reporter, with reporter defaulting to nil), -262 (reporters held weakly so a window closed mid-flick cannot pin the app to scrolling, plus the ScrollActivityReporter protocol shape), -263 (the at-most-one watchdog, its sleep-first 2 second period, the snapshot sweep, the drop rule, the republish and the self-clearing exit), -264 (the not-scrolling transition cancels the task and nils the handle, with cancellation observed in the while condition and the post-sleep guard). PR-SETTINGS-263 also records the latent hazard that reporting true with the default nil reporter would get the timeline swept after 2 seconds, and that no caller in the pinned tree does this. Ownership note for the merge: findings 14 and 49 name CHAT and THEME as owners of the same file, so a reviewer should confirm the CHAT/THEME repair pass did not add a duplicate of the same contract.

resolutions.finding: Missing 47 - LimitHandoff.swift:1-78 is entirely unspecified, with eleven verbatim strings and several caps; "USAGE should own it".
resolutions.truth: LimitHandoff is transitively dead, so under the contract rule "Dead code gets no requirement" it must NOT become a USAGE requirement. Proof, all in the pinned tree: a repository-wide grep for LimitHandoff returns only its own declaration at LimitHandoff.swift:6 and the single call at AutoContinue.swift:80 inside `func handOff(_ threadID: UUID)` (:78); a grep for handOff returns AutoContinue.swift:78/:80, the unrelated AppUpdater.swift:270/:373 pair, and exactly one caller, LimitResumeBadge.swift:31; a grep for LimitResumeBadge returns exactly one hit, its own declaration at LimitResumeBadge.swift:5. dead_code.md entry 21 already proves LimitResumeBadge dead and entry 22 already proves AutoContinue.handOff dead. The critic's own finding 40 says the same thing and contradicts finding 47.
resolutions.action_taken: none. No requirement added to USAGE.json. The correct remedy is a dead_code.md entry for LimitHandoff.swift, which finding 40 already asks for and which is outside my editable file set.

new_upstream_defects: DroppyCode/App/Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift:48-60 - SettingsPage.tint declares nine colours and NOTHING in the pinned tree reads the property. The sidebar builds every row from title and symbol only (:143-152); a repository-wide grep for a reader returns none (the `.tint` hits at SettingsView.swift:464, AboutUpdateViews.swift:660 and ShortcutsSettingsPage.swift:436 are the SwiftUI environment tint, standing.tint and session.tint respectively), and SettingsPage is referenced outside its own file only by WindowManager.showSettings(page:) at WindowManager.swift:32. It is dead and has no entry in dead_code.md. Realistic worst outcome: a Windows port reproduces nine sRGB triples that paint no pixel, and, worse, a reviewer reading PR-SETTINGS-007's old title ("used by the command palette and anything else asking for a page's colour") expects tinted settings sidebar rows and files the correct, untinted port as a parity failure. I corrected PR-SETTINGS-007 in SETTINGS.json; the dead_code.md entry is still owed and that file is outside my editable set.

DroppyCode/UI/Common/RenderBudget.swift:30 - setScrolling's `reporter` parameter defaults to nil, so `setScrolling(true, timeline: id)` is a legal call that registers an active timeline with no reporter. The watchdog at :49-54 then drops that timeline on its first 2 second sweep because `reporters[id]?.object` is nil, un-pausing every animation while the reader is still scrolling. No caller in the pinned tree does this (SettingsScrollTracker.swift:25 and ThreadTimeline.swift:1037 both pass reporter: self), so it is latent rather than shipped, but the signature invites it. Realistic worst outcome: a port adds one start report without a reporter and scroll-pausing silently stops working app-wide after two seconds. Recorded in PR-SETTINGS-263's windows_path.

DroppyCode/App/Runtime/LimitHandoff.swift:1-78 - the whole file is transitively dead (only caller AutoContinue.swift:80, whose only caller LimitResumeBadge.swift:31 is proven dead by dead_code.md entry 21) yet has no dead_code.md entry, unlike its two callers. Not strictly new (critic finding 40 raises it) but it is still unrecorded in the ledger. Realistic worst outcome: a later reader treats the silence as an omission and ports eleven user-visible strings and four caps that no user can reach, or conversely a future port of LimitResumeBadge reinstates the badge without the handoff payload.
consequential_candidates: DroppyCode/Core/Models/Library.swift:248 - hasCustomTitle decodes to false on a missing, null or wrong-typed key. Faithful reproduction means a thread the user deliberately renamed, whose flag is unreadable in library.json, is treated as still auto-titled and has the user's chosen name silently overwritten by the automatic titler on its next turn. That is irreversible loss of user-entered data with no prompt and no undo. It is upstream-designed behaviour and I specified it as-is in PR-STORE-156 (which states the consequence explicitly), but it is the one decode default in this set whose faithful reproduction destroys something the user typed, so it should be an owner decision rather than a silent port.

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Library.swift:254 - isInPanel decodes to false, which is the SHOWN state. This is the safe direction and I flag it only as the inverse risk: a port that guesses true, or that reverses the sense of the flag, removes the thread from the sidebar, the command palette, the recent picks and the unread count at once, so the work looks deleted while the record is intact. PR-STORE-162 names this; it is listed here because the failure is silent and total rather than because the source is wrong.

DroppyCode/Core/Models/Library.swift:255 - expandsHelpers is persisted, its computed inverse foldsHelpers (:167-170) is not. A port that persists the inverse under the same key flips the fold state of every existing chat on first load. Not data loss, but a silent, repository-wide change to saved user state on upgrade. Recorded in PR-STORE-163's windows_path.
